intro: A feeling about what another person does takes the subjunctive, even when the fact is true.
p.me alegro de que.consejo: It has «de» before «que». You can also say «me alegra que», without «de».
p.qué pena que.consejo: It is an exclamation. It has no «me»: «¡qué pena que no vengas!». It ends in the subjunctive.
p.siento que.consejo: Here «sentir» means to regret, not to notice. «Siento que no puedas venir» is an apology.
p.me molesta que.consejo: What bothers is what comes after «que», so «molesta» stays singular.
p.me encanta que.consejo: Stronger than «me gusta que». Both ask for the subjunctive if the person changes.
p.me sorprende que.consejo: It works for good and bad surprises. The fact can be true: it still takes the subjunctive.
p.me da miedo que.consejo: You use «dar miedo», not «tener miedo»: «me da miedo que llegues tarde».
p.me extraña que.consejo: The ñ sounds «ny»: «eks-TRA-nya». Do not mix it up with «extranjero».
p.qué bien que.consejo: A short, very common exclamation: «¡qué bien que vengas!».
p.qué raro que.consejo: It expresses surprise: «¡qué raro que no llame!». It also takes the subjunctive.
p.puntual.consejo: It works for a man and a woman. The opposite is «impuntual». Say «pun-TWAL».
p.gente.consejo: It is singular: «la gente llega», not «la gente llegan». The g sounds like h.
b1.titulo: Feeling something about what another does
b1.texto:
When a sentence expresses a **feeling** and what causes it is done by **another person**, the verb goes in the **subjunctive**:

- **Me alegro de que** estés aquí.
- ¡**Qué pena que** no puedas venir!
- **Me molesta que** fumen.
- **Me extraña que** no llame.

The fact can be **true**: you are here, they smoke. You use the subjunctive because you **react** to the fact; you are not reporting it.

If the one who feels and the one who acts are the **same person**, use the infinitive: **me alegro de estar** aquí, **siento llegar** tarde.
b2.f0.texto: How great that you are here!
b2.f1.texto: I am sorry Ana cannot come.
b2.f2.texto: I find it odd that she does not call.
b2.f3.texto: It bothers me when people arrive late.
b2.f4.texto: And I love it that you are so punctual.
b2.f5.texto: I am glad to be here with you.
b2.f6.texto: I am afraid the night will end so soon.
b2.f7.texto: How strange that nobody wants to leave.
b4.texto:
Feeling expressions group like this:

- **Joy and liking**: me alegro de que · me alegra que · me encanta que · me gusta que · qué bien que.
- **Sadness, annoyance and fear**: siento que · qué pena que · me molesta que · me da miedo que.
- **Surprise**: me sorprende que · me extraña que · qué raro que.

They all follow the same pattern: **feeling + que + subjunctive** if the subject changes, and **feeling + infinitive** if the subject is the same.

Watch the preposition: **alegrarse de** (me alegro de que), but **me alegra que**, without «de».
b4.e0.texto: I am glad that you are here.
b4.e1.texto: It bothers me that people smoke here.
b4.e2.texto: I am sorry to be late.
b5.f0.texto: The train slowly enters the station under a cloud of steam.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía waits on the platform with her coat open and her hands restless.
b5.f2.texto: The loudspeakers repeat the name of the city in a metallic voice.
b5.f3.texto: A cold breeze lifts the dry leaves from the ground.
b5.f4.texto: Each door of the train opens with a long sigh.
b5.f5.texto: Among the crowd Ana appears with a small suitcase.
b5.f6.texto: Her tired smile lights up the whole platform.
b5.f7.texto: Lucía runs towards her and hugs her with moist eyes.
b5.f8.texto: The two of them walk together under the yellow lights of the street.
b5.f9.texto: The night air smells of nearby rain and freshly baked bread.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! It is a reaction to what another does: subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Estás» reports the fact. With a feeling comes the subjunctive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive only works if the one who feels is the one who is there.
b6.pregunta: Pablo's visit makes you glad. What is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: The fact is not doubtful: they really smoke. The cause is different.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That's it! A feeling about what another does asks for the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It speaks of the present. The tense does not explain the subjunctive.
b7.pregunta: Why does «me molesta que fumen» take the subjunctive?
b8.o0.refuerzo: That would be another person arriving. Here it is you.
b8.o1.refuerzo: «Llego» is conjugated. Here the infinitive is needed.
b8.pregunta: You yourself arrive late. What is missing?
b9.frase: Me extraña que Ana no llame
b9.traduccion: I find it odd that Ana does not call
b10.o0: Me da miedo que se vaya.
b10.o2: Me alegro de que se vaya.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I am glad you are here» (tú).
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Puedes» reports the fact. After «qué pena que» comes the subjunctive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Poder» becomes «pueda» in the subjunctive.
b12.o2.refuerzo: After «que» you need a conjugated verb.
b12.pregunta: Your friend cannot come. What is missing?
p.pueda.consejo: Subjunctive of «poder» for yo, él or usted. The o becomes ue, just like in «puedo».
p.llame.consejo: Subjunctive of «llamar» for yo, él or usted. The ll sounds y: «YA-me».
p.llegue.consejo: Subjunctive of «llegar». «Gu» keeps the g sound and the u is silent: «YE-ge».
p.seas.consejo: Subjunctive of «ser» for tú. It is irregular: not from «eres». The e and a are separate syllables.
p.alegro.consejo: From «alegrarse» (to be glad), always with «me»: «me alegro de que…». It comes from «alegre».
p.termine.consejo: Subjunctive of «terminar». It is an -ar verb: the a of «termina» becomes e: «termine».
p.quiera.consejo: Subjunctive of «querer». The e becomes ie, like «quiero». The qu sounds k.
p.fume.consejo: Subjunctive of «fumar». It comes from «humo» (smoke). Verbs in -ar change a to e.
p.nube.consejo: It is feminine: «la nube». The plural is «nubes». «Una nube de vapor» is a lot of steam together.
p.vapor.consejo: The v sounds b and the stress is on the last syllable: «ba-POR». Plural: «vapores».
p.inquietas.consejo: Feminine plural of «inquieto». The qu sounds k: «in-KYE-tas». Its opposite is «tranquilas».
p.altavoces.consejo: Plural of «altavoz»: the z changes to c. The c sounds th: «al-ta-BO-thes».
p.repiten.consejo: The e becomes i in «repiten» but not in «repetimos». The initial r sounds strong.
p.metálica.consejo: The accent is on the «ta»: «me-TA-li-ka». Feminine of «metálico», for «voz» or «puerta».
p.secas.consejo: Feminine plural of «seco». The c sounds k before a: «SE-kas». Its opposite is «mojadas».
p.suspiro.consejo: The verb is «suspirar». You can sigh from sadness, tiredness or relief: «un suspiro largo».
p.aparece.consejo: The c sounds th: «a-pa-RE-the». With «yo» it becomes «aparezco», like «conozco».
p.ilumina.consejo: It comes from «luz» (light). A smile can also «iluminar» a face or a place.
p.húmedos.consejo: The h is silent and the accent is on the «u»: «U-me-dos». «Ojos húmedos» are eyes full of tears.
p.juntas.consejo: The j sounds h: «HUN-tas». Here it describes «las dos»: it agrees in gender and number.
p.cercana.consejo: From «cerca» (near). Both c's are different: the first sounds th, the second k.
p.reaccionas.consejo: The initial r sounds strong and «cc» sounds «kth»: «rre-ak-THYO-nas». It means to answer to something.
p.sentimiento.consejo: It comes from «sentir». «Ie» is one syllable: «sen-ti-MYEN-to». Plural: «sentimientos».
p.puedas.consejo: Subjunctive of «poder» for tú. The o becomes ue, just like in «puedes».
